hints: As you walk through nums, what do you need to remember to notice that a value has turned up before?
Keep a hash set of values already seen. The moment you meet a value that is already in the set, a repeat exists and you can return true.

1. Start an empty set.
  2. For each value: if it is in the set, return true.
  3. Otherwise add it to the set.
  4. If the loop ends with no hit, return false.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Compare every pair of positions for equal values.

approaches.name: Better
approaches.idea: Sort the array; any repeat ends up next to its twin, so check neighbours.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: One pass with a HashSet; add returning false means the value was already there.

explain: For nums = [1, 2, 3, 1] the set grows to {1, 2, 3}. When the last 1 arrives it is already in the set, so the function returns true. In Java, set.add(x) returns false when x was present, which gives the check for free. Values range up to ±109, so a counting array will not work; a hash set handles any range.
recognize: "Does anything appear twice?" → remember what you have seen in a hash set.
javascript: function containsDuplicate(nums) { const a = [...nums].sort((x, y) => x - y); for (let i = 1; i < a.length; i++) if (a[i] === a[i - 1]) return true; return false; }
